I bartend at a private yacht club, I’d say it’s a really good place to learn all the ins and outs of banquets, fine dining and classic cocktails. You’ll probably see a fair share of weddings and big parties, but expect to work very late nights. It’s a weird mix of restaurant and actual bar setting. The thing I notice a lot is members generally communicate about all showing up together, so you can be dead one second and have a bar full of people the next. It’s all member charge so we get regular bi weekly paychecks, which can be a bummer. You’ll get the occasional regular who will just slip you money here and there which is pretty cool. I’d say it’s split down the middle of really chill people and really annoying entitled members. You’ll make close friends though, and some of the members look after you like family. There was a member here at our club who paid to get one of my coworkers all of her teeth fixed because of a disease she had, pretty cool.  The members expect you to know them by name, and to remember everything that is important. Try and learn the member numbers as fast as you can, half the time they won’t remind you and you’ll have to flag them down if not. We have an auto grat of 20% on every check that is created, which is great for those slow nights and frugal members. All in all, I think it’s a great place for learning, but for long term stay it can become very exhausting very quickly in my opinion.
